messages.content: The client just moved the workshop to their King of Prussia office. I did complete the Notary and Delta bookings after our last chat, but the hotel is still refundable through tomorrow evening. Can you compare keeping it with moving closer to the new site?
Yes. What is the office address or nearest landmark, and should I compare rideshares only or include a rental car?
It’s near 1000 Continental Drive. Include rideshares and a rental car, but I would rather not drive if the costs are reasonably close.

I found three available suburban options under the nightly cap. The strongest is the Sheraton Valley Forge, about 2 miles from the office, at $214 per night and $742.36 total for August 10–13. The Element Valley Forge is $226 per night, $781.42 total, about 1.5 miles away. Hyatt House King of Prussia is $231 per night, $798.17 total, about 3 miles away. All three are cancelable without charge through tomorrow evening.
Compare the Sheraton with keeping the Notary. Include the airport trips and all three workshop days.

Keeping the Notary: the room remains $828.14. A rideshare from PHL to the hotel is about $32–$44. The weekday trip to Continental Drive is roughly 35–65 minutes in the morning and $52–$74 each way; returning downtown can take 45–75 minutes. Across six workshop rides, plus the two airport rides, estimated transportation is $376–$532. Combined hotel and local transportation: about $1,204–$1,360.

At the Sheraton, PHL rideshares are about $64–$82 each way and usually take 30–45 minutes outside the worst traffic. The office rides are approximately $10–$16 each way and 5–12 minutes. Six office rides plus both airport transfers total about $188–$260. With the $742.36 room total, the combined estimate is $930–$1,002.
So even with the more expensive airport rides, moving saves money?
Yes. The suburban plan is about $274–$358 less overall, and it removes roughly three to six hours of accumulated commuting risk over the workshop. The hotel itself is also $85.78 cheaper.
What does the rental-car version look like?

A compact car from Monday night through Thursday evening is currently about $238–$286 including estimated taxes. The Sheraton has complimentary parking, and fuel plus tolls should add around $25–$35. That puts ground transportation near $263–$321. It is somewhat more than the suburban rideshare estimate and requires driving after the evening arrival, so rideshare is the better fit unless prices surge substantially.
Agreed. Before changing it, confirm that the Delta flights stay untouched and that canceling the Notary has no penalty.

Confirmed: the Delta Main Cabin itinerary remains Monday 5:18–8:52 p.m. MSP–PHL and Thursday 9:05–10:48 p.m. PHL–MSP; no flight action is involved. The Notary reservation shows cancellation permitted through tomorrow at 6:00 p.m. Philadelphia time with a full refund to the corporate card. No prepaid or nonrefundable charge is listed.
Go ahead and switch to the Sheraton standard king at $742.36. Keep rideshares as the transportation plan.

Done. The Notary reservation has been canceled with a full refund of $828.14 pending to the original corporate card. The Sheraton Valley Forge standard king is confirmed for August 10–13 at $742.36 including estimated taxes, with no deposit and payment at checkout. Free cancellation runs through tomorrow at 6:00 p.m. local time. The Delta flights are unchanged, and the working transportation estimate is $188–$260 for airport and workshop rideshares.
